records.summary: The look of a control is its appearance; type named it before the axes were split.
sf-alert's look is its appearance, not a variant.
What an alert or a toast reports is its status; type answered that question before the axes were split.
A progress indicator's colour role is its status.
What a component is made of is its kind.
records.manual: sf-tree-item also reads type from its item data (_sourceData.type); write kind there too.

records.summary: What a component is made of is its kind, not a variant.
sf-tag's type answered two questions: a kind (checkbox, icon, color, avatar, default) and a status (info, success, warning, error). Each now has its own axis.
records.manual: Write kind= when the value is checkbox, icon, color, avatar or default, and status= when it is info, success, warning or error.

records.summary: sf-badge's scheme carried statuses; status is the axis now.
records.manual: Move a status value (info, success, warning, error) from scheme= to status=; a colour scheme value stays where it is.

records.summary: Every field takes its size from one attribute, size.
Icon positions are logical, so they follow the writing direction.
Inner spacing is one profile, spacing, with named values.
records.manual: tightness=low becomes spacing=compact, default (or empty) becomes normal, high becomes comfortable, highest becomes spacious.

records.summary: size names the size ladder everywhere; a file's byte size is file-size.
Classes for the gallery's lightbox are lightbox-class; class and root-class belong to the element itself.
The scrollbar's mode is data-mode.
One word for a failure across the Framework: error.
The status without a meaning is neutral; components had their own words for it.
A file preview that picks its look by itself is auto.
A tag with a count is a default tag with count=.
records.manual: Keep the number in count=.

records.summary: The drawer is on the shared size ladder.

records.manual: Only where the page may be right-to-left does the difference show: left stays on the left there, inline-start moves to the right.

records.summary: Context menu positions name a side and an edge in one vocabulary.

records.manual: sf-range-slider-change also fired when a value was set from code; change does not. Code that relied on the event after a programmatic set calls its handler itself.

records.manual: sf-upgrade --apply rewrites a declaration of a format: in a JSON file that keeps the standard layout (JSON.stringify with two or four spaces, or tabs), every "schema": "simai.<name>.v<major>" becomes "schema": "simai.<name>" with "schema_version": <major> right after it; in a script, a literal schema: 'simai.<name>.v<major>' (or 'schema' => '...' in PHP) gains schema_version beside it when the file names schema_version nowhere else. What it reports and leaves: a comparison against the label (a reader of your own: read both forms until remove_after with readSchema or isSchema from core/js/composition/schema-name.mjs), a JSON file in another layout, and every format an item marks held -- the Framework itself keeps those in the older form for the reason given, so leave them until the item is released.

records.summary: sf-theme-generator's events are sf-theme-generator-change and sf-theme-generator-apply; their first names, sf-theme-change and sf-theme-apply, clash with the Loader's light/dark event and are emitted beside them until the sweep. The runtime's own names on window.SF -- the message bus, the runtime module registry's own state, the Smart base's announcement and litHtml -- live under SF.__internal; the old names read and write through to it, noted as deprecated, until the sweep. records.manual: Nothing a page needs is here: use the public API (core/contracts/public-js-api.json). Code of the Framework's own reads SF.__internal.<name>.

records.summary: A composition value type is named without a version: record-changed, record-removed, collection-changed, files-moved, counter, navigation, preference-changed, record-id, record-ids, text and boolean, in place of the older labels record-changed.v1 and the rest. Both forms are read until remove_after, so a host, a component and a page may move one at a time; a route between a bare name and its older label already works.

records.summary: SF.Effects.EFFECT_SCHEMA held the older label of the effect format, simai.effect.v1, and was described as the label a writer emits, against format-names-without-version. records.manual: Where code writes {schema: SF.Effects.EFFECT_SCHEMA, ...} (or imports EFFECT_SCHEMA from core/js/effects.js), write {...SF.Effects.EFFECT_FORMAT, ...}. records.summary: The class unit ajax is removed. It was one re-export of the legacy system's SF.Ajax helper, built as a second copy that no Loader rule loaded and nothing imported.

To load a part of the page, use the Smart component sf-include (src, load="now" or "view"). deprecated_on and remove_after are the policy's dates for the day of the removal and mean nothing further: no Loader rule ever loaded the unit, so there was no alias to keep.

records.manual: Load the content with fetch() when the element enters the viewport (an IntersectionObserver), or use the Smart component sf-include (src, load="view"), which ships in the same pair; sf-fragment is the core's fragment boundary, not a loader. [sf-canceltrack] has no successor: an observer stops by itself after the first load. Bitrix sites keep their own frozen copy of the unit. deprecated_on and remove_after are the policy's dates for the day of the removal and mean nothing further: no Loader rule ever loaded the unit, so there was no alias to keep.

records.summary: The SIMAI Framework Pro component package (sf-table, sf-data-view, sf-property-view, sf-admin-menu and the rest built from simai/ui-pro) is named pro, not larena; Larena is one of its consumers. The Loader takes the old name as a dated alias until remove_after: SF_BOOT_CONFIG.packages.larena declares the same package as packages.pro (the same base, the same rule file), and a package built under the old name, whose rule file calls SF.RuleLoader.registerPackage('larena', ...), registers as pro. Each use is noted in SF.deprecations. When a page declares both names, pro is used and larena is said aloud and ignored. The tags, rules, attributes, events and ports are unchanged.
records.manual: Write pro for larena in the page's package declaration (SF_BOOT_CONFIG.packages.pro, or 'packages' => ['pro' => [...]] in a PHP config) and take a package built as pro (pro-<12>, package-pro.tar, wave-1/output/package/pro): its rule file calls registerPackage('pro'). The base may stay where it is served. A Framework pair from before this record knows only the name the page declares, so a page and the package it loads move together: either both say larena (an older pair) or the page says pro over this pair or later, where both builds work.

records.summary: The background system's naming scheme (C16, owner-approved 2026-11-08; role, variant, state): 51 theme roles take purpose names -- surface-0 and surface-1 are surface-page and surface-area, elevation-1/3/4--surface are surface-card, surface-popup and surface-popup-nested (their shadows and dim ink likewise), <colour>-transparent-hover/select/active are <colour>-state-*, <colour>-transparent-overlay is <colour>-container-strong, surface-overlay is surface-veil, outline-<colour> is <colour>-outline, disable and on-disable are surface-disabled and on-surface-disabled. Values do not change: each former name is var() of its new name, declared on the theme root and on every rule that re-declares the role. Elevation 2 and 5 and the four shadow--* names are held (token-aliases.v1.json, held).

Twenty public component variables that set a fill end in -background-color, as the other 53 do (C16 naming): --sf-card-background is --sf-card-background-color, and so on for alert-bar, code, contents, figure, kbd, list-attention, pager, procedure, progress-run, search, site-header, tile-metric, wizard and workspace-drawer. The component reads the new name first and the former one under it, so a page that sets the former name draws as before.

The background utilities take the C16 names beside the former ones: bg-surface-page, -area, -card, -popup and -popup-nested (the place classes also declare --sf-surface-place and the place's dim ink), bg-<colour>-state-select, bg-<colour>-container-strong, bg-surface-veil, bg-surface-disabled, hover:/active:bg-<colour>-state. The former classes paint the same colour until remove_after.

The shadow system (C20, owner-approved 2026-11-08): four shadows by place -- --sf-shadow-flat, --sf-shadow-raised, --sf-shadow-overlay, --sf-shadow-modal, from --sf-shadow-key-color and --sf-shadow-ambient-color -- replace the numbered levels (--sf-elevation-N--shadow, --sf-ui-shadow-N), the upward layer style and the three shadow colours. Level 1 is raised, 2 and 3 overlay, 4 and 5 modal; the C16 names --sf-shadow-card, -popup and -popup-nested are raised, overlay and overlay. Level 2's and 5's surfaces and dim ink, held by C16, join popup and popup-nested. Each former name is var() of its successor on the theme root; the value follows the place, a visible change approved as C20 (light theme one key and one ambient layer at black 16 and 8, dark theme the key at 28 and no ambient).

records.summary: The numbered patterns pattern-1 ... pattern-9 (SF4's bg-p3, p4, p1, p2, p16, p11, p12, p20, p13, and their sm: ... xxl: forms) are deprecated and draw unchanged until remove_after. They were 2-4 px black pixel tiles set with the background shorthand, so they wiped the element's own background, took no colour, vanished on a dark surface and shimmered at fractional screen scaling. Owner decision C57 (2026-11-11): they are replaced by the six patterns of the pattern utility; the dispatcher (2026-11-11) keeps them for the usual transition, since ui-doc and consumers still use them. Each item names the nearest new pattern; the look is not the same, so the rewrite is manual. The breakpoint forms have no new counterpart: a pattern does not change with the breakpoint.
records.manual: Replace the class with pattern-<shape> and, where wanted, pattern-color-<role|hue>, pattern-strength-8|12|16|24, pattern-size-<space step> and pattern-fade-none|spot|clear|down (standard simai.backgrounds, Patterns). The nearest shapes: pattern-1, -2 and -8 (lines, maze) pattern-grid; pattern-3, -6 and -7 (dots, blocks) pattern-dots; pattern-4 and -9 (checker, blocks) pattern-checker; pattern-5 (diagonals) pattern-hatch. The new layer lies under the content and keeps the element's background. Used over a photo to darken it, use a gradient scrim or the C16 glass instead.

records.summary: The stripe utilities join the patterns (owner decision C60, 2026-11-11): stripe-3 (lines both ways) is pattern-grid and stripe-4 (135-degree lines) is pattern-hatch, drawn right: a vector tile, a 1.25 px line, the colour a role at an alpha step and a layer under the content. stripe-1 and stripe-2 (lines one way) have no pattern of their own. The colours stripe-<role> become pattern-color-<role> with a pattern-strength, the sizes stripe-size-1 ... 4 (2 to 5 px primitives) a step of the space ladder, pattern-size-<step>. records.manual: Replace stripe-3 with pattern-grid and stripe-4 with pattern-hatch; a colour stripe-<role> with pattern-color-<role> and a strength (pattern-strength-8|12|16|24; the stripe drew the role at full strength), a size stripe-size-N with pattern-size-<space step>. stripe-1, stripe-2, stripe-transparent, stripe-current and stripe-inherit have no successor: draw the lines in the component's own sheet, or take pattern-grid. records.summary: A theme is the four dynamic palettes -- primary, secondary, tertiary, neutral -- and no status palette (docs study 2026-11-11 TG-01). Core declares --sf-error-*, --sf-warning-*, --sf-success-* and --sf-info-* as var() of the static hues red, amber, green and blue (C17, C90, C100); themeFromColor and themeFromHct wrote them as literal colours too, so a page themed by sf-theme-generator, sf-input-color variant theme or applyTheme froze the statuses at the hues of the day (a theme made before a status hue moved would keep the old one). Now theme.palettes holds four palettes, THEME_PALETTES and THEME_ALPHA name four, and themeVariables, themeToCss and applyTheme write 144 variables (64 tones, 80 translucent steps) where they wrote 288. A theme object stored with eight palettes applies only its four theme palettes. The former API keeps working until 2027-01-01 with a warning: a status override in the options is ignored (option-theme-status-override) and theme.palettes.<status> reads the static hue (property-theme-status-palettes).

items.to: the static hue STATUS_HUES[status] (staticPalette()); theme.palettes.<status> reads it with a warning until 2027-01-01

records.manual: Code that read theme.palettes.error (or warning, success, info) reads SF.ThemePalette.staticPalette()[SF.ThemePalette.STATUS_HUES.error] instead. A site stylesheet written by themeToCss or the generator before this pair carries the status tones as literal values: drop its --sf-error-*, --sf-warning-*, --sf-success-* and --sf-info-* lines (or make the theme again) so core's static hues apply. A status colour of a site's own is not a theme: there is none, the statuses are fixed (C17).

records.summary: A grey colour makes a grey theme (C16, docs study 2026-11-11 TG-03). colorToHct took a colour as vivid as its hue holds at its tone for the vivid palette (chroma 85); at black and white the gamut holds no chroma, so #000000 made a pink theme (hue 0, chroma 85) and #ffffff a teal one. A colour under HCT chroma 5 (the neutral palette's chroma) now keeps its own chroma, and its secondary and tertiary palettes take that chroma instead of 20 and 40 -- a near-black like #111111 (hue 209) no longer gets bluish secondary containers. Every colour at chroma 5 or more, the Framework's own #005bbe among them, makes the same theme as before.
records.manual: Nothing to rewrite. A site whose stored brand colour is black, white or a near-grey and whose theme was written as CSS before this pair makes the theme again to drop the tinted palettes.

records.summary: A status palette in the options of themeFromColor or themeFromHct ({error|warning|success|info: {hue, chroma}}) no longer makes a theme palette: the statuses are core's static hues (C17, C90) and a theme holds four palettes (behaviour-theme-writes-no-status-palette). records.manual: Remove the status keys from the options. A status colour of a site's own does not exist: the four statuses are fixed (C17).

records.summary: theme.palettes.error, .warning, .success and .info of a theme (themeFromColor, themeFromHct, sf-theme-generator's theme value, toJSON() and detail.theme) are not part of the theme any more (behaviour-theme-writes-no-status-palette). records.summary: Owner decision C212 (6): one set to hide -- hidden (display), invisible (visibility), sr-only with not-sr-only (now in the core sheet, there at the first paint) and on paper print-hidden, print-only, print-invisible. records.manual: Write print-only for print-block, print-inline, print-inline-block, print-flex, print-inline-flex and print-table; when the element must take a display on paper other than its own, set it in a page rule under @media print.
